meta.name: Assess visa eligibility and send PDF checklists with Claude and SendGrid

name: AI Visa Eligibility Agent - Passport OCR, Rule Check, Checklist & PDF Delivery

parameters.content:
## AI Visa Eligibility Agent

This workflow reads an applicant's passport, extracts their nationality and passport details, checks visa rules for their chosen destination and purpose of travel, recommends a visa type, generates a document checklist, turns it into a PDF, and emails it to the applicant — with every request logged for review.

The visa-rule and eligibility judgment is AI-driven (rules and policy vary by country, purpose, and change over time, so this is not hard-coded), but document extraction validation and checklist assembly are kept deterministic where possible so results are explainable and reproducible.

### Who's it for
- Travel agencies and visa consultancies wanting a first-pass automated intake and pre-screening layer
- Immigration advisors who want obviously-simple cases (e.g. visa-free short tourist stays) resolved instantly, so they only spend time on complex cases
- Anyone replacing manual visa-rule lookup and checklist emails with automation

### How it works
1. Applicant submits their details, destination, travel purpose, and raw OCR text extracted from their passport bio page via webhook POST
2. AI reads the passport text, extracts structured data (name, nationality, passport number, expiry), and cross-checks it against what the applicant declared
3. Applications with unreadable or clearly incomplete passport data get an immediate resubmission request instead of proceeding
4. AI reviews the extracted nationality, destination, purpose, and stay length, and returns whether a visa is required, the visa category, a recommended visa type, processing time, and any eligibility risks
5. Code assembles a document checklist from a standard base list plus purpose-specific items (business, study, work, family visit, transit) plus any AI-flagged risks
6. Code renders the assessment and checklist as HTML, which is converted to a PDF via an external PDF-generation API
7. Every application is logged to Google Sheets regardless of outcome
8. The applicant is emailed their assessment with the checklist PDF attached
9. Webhook responds with the full assessment as JSON

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add Anthropic Claude credentials and attach to both Anthropic model nodes
3. Sign up for an HTML-to-PDF API (e.g. PDFShift, Api2Pdf, DocRaptor) and replace the URL and YOUR_PDF_API_KEY in HTTP Request - Generate Checklist PDF; adjust the response parsing to match your chosen provider's output format
4. Add SendGrid credentials and replace YOUR_SENDGRID_API_KEY / YOUR_TOKEN_HERE in the email node
5. Replace loans@yourlender.com style sender address with your own
6. Switch the Google Sheets HTTP node to the native Google Sheets node with OAuth2, or add OAuth2 credentials directly, and replace YOUR_SHEET_ID
7. Set up your Google Sheet with a VisaApplications tab (column layout below)
8. Activate and POST a test application to the webhook URL

### Requirements
- Anthropic Claude API key (claude-sonnet-4 recommended)
- An HTML-to-PDF conversion API
- SendGrid API key for email delivery
- Google Sheets with OAuth2 credentials (VisaApplications tab)
- n8n instance with a publicly accessible webhook URL

### How to customize
- Replace the raw passport-text field with a real OCR step (e.g. fetch an uploaded passport image, then call an OCR API) ahead of Stage 1
- Add a real-time visa-rules lookup tool (e.g. a visa requirements API or web search tool) to the Stage 2 agent for higher accuracy than the model's built-in knowledge alone
- Adjust the base and purpose-specific checklist items in JS - Generate Document Checklist to match your consultancy's standard requirements
- Raise or lower the passport verification threshold in IF - Passport Data Sufficient (default: score >= 4)
- Add a second AI reviewer call for high-risk destinations as a maker-checker control

### Important note
This workflow produces a preparatory assessment and checklist, not an official visa decision. Visa rules change frequently and vary by consulate. Always direct applicants to confirm current requirements with the destination country's official embassy, consulate, or immigration authority before they apply.

### Google Sheets Column Layout

VisaApplications tab - row 1 headers:
Application ID | Applicant Name | Applicant Email | Destination Country | Travel Purpose | Nationality | Visa Required | Visa Category | Recommended Visa Type | Confidence | Decided At

## Stage 1: Intake & Passport OCR Extraction

Accepts visa eligibility requests via webhook POST, including raw extracted text from the applicant's passport bio page. All fields have sensible defaults so the workflow can be tested without a payload.

The extraction AI (claude-sonnet-4, temperature 0.2 for accuracy) reads the passport text and extracts structured data, cross-checking it against the applicant's self-reported name and nationality, flagging any inconsistencies or unreadable fields.

JS - Parse Passport Extraction Output extracts the AI JSON with a lenient fallback that trusts the applicant's self-reported nationality if parsing fails.

IF - Passport Data Sufficient sends an immediate resubmission request for unreadable or clearly incomplete passport scans, instead of proceeding with bad data.

## Stage 2: Visa Rule Check & Recommendation

A Wait buffer respects API rate limits before this call.

The visa-rules AI (claude-sonnet-4, temperature 0.3 for consistent, grounded judgment) reviews the applicant's extracted nationality, destination, purpose, and stay length, then determines whether a visa is required, the visa category, and a recommended visa type.

It also returns an estimated processing time, any eligibility risks (e.g. insufficient passport validity, purpose mismatch), a plain-language reasoning grounded in the details provided, a pointer to verify with the official embassy/consulate, and a confidence level.

JS - Parse Eligibility Output extracts that JSON with a cautious fallback: if parsing fails, the application defaults to a 'consult embassy' recommendation with low confidence rather than a silent visa-free assumption.

## Stage 3: Checklist, PDF & Delivery

JS - Generate Document Checklist combines a standard base checklist with purpose-specific items (Business, Study, Work, Family Visit, Transit) and any AI-flagged eligibility risks.

JS - Build Checklist PDF HTML renders the full assessment and checklist as clean HTML.

HTTP Request - Generate Checklist PDF converts that HTML to a PDF via an external HTML-to-PDF API (replace with your provider of choice).

JS - Format Final Application Record assembles the complete decision object and the summary row for the tracker sheet.

Save Application to Google Sheets Tracker appends that row — every application is logged, regardless of outcome.

Send Applicant Email with Checklist PDF delivers the assessment and attaches the generated checklist PDF.

The webhook then responds with the full assessment as JSON.

parameters.text:
=You are a meticulous passport document verification specialist.

Applicant declared:
Name: {{ $json.applicantName }}
Self-Reported Nationality: {{ $json.nationality }}

Passport bio page (raw extracted text):
{{ $json.passportOcrText }}

Your task:
1. Extract structured data from the passport text.
2. Cross-check the extracted name and nationality against what the applicant declared.
3. Flag if the passport text is missing, illegible, incomplete, or looks inconsistent, and flag if the passport will expire soon (less than 6 months from today).

Return a JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
{
  "passportReadable": true or false,
  "extractedFullName": "Full name found on the passport",
  "extractedNationality": "Nationality found on the passport",
  "extractedPassportNumber": "Passport number found on the passport",
  "extractedDOB": "Date of birth found on the passport",
  "extractedExpiryDate": "Passport expiry date found on the passport",
  "monthsUntilExpiry": <number, estimated months of validity remaining from today>,
  "consistencyIssues": ["issue1", "issue2"],
  "extractionNotes": "Brief summary of the verification outcome",
  "extractionScore": <number 1-10, 10 = fully readable, consistent, verifiable passport data>
}

If no consistency issues are found, return an empty array. Return ONLY the JSON. No markdown, no explanation.

parameters.responseBody:
={
  "success": false,
  "applicationId": "{{ $json.applicationId }}",
  "status": "Passport Not Readable",
  "extractionNotes": "{{ $json.extractionNotes }}",
  "consistencyIssues": {{ JSON.stringify($json.consistencyIssues) }},
  "message": "We could not read your passport details clearly. Please resubmit a clear scan or photo of your passport bio page."
}

nodes.name: AI - Check Visa Rules & Suggest Visa Type

parameters.text:
=You are a visa eligibility research assistant helping a human travel advisor, not issuing a final visa decision.

Traveler nationality (from passport): {{ $json.extractedNationality }}
Destination country: {{ $json.destinationCountry }}
Purpose of travel: {{ $json.travelPurpose }}
Intended arrival date: {{ $json.intendedArrivalDate }}
Intended length of stay: {{ $json.intendedStayDays }} days
Passport expiry: {{ $json.extractedExpiryDate }} (~{{ $json.monthsUntilExpiry }} months of validity remaining)
Document consistency issues: {{ JSON.stringify($json.consistencyIssues) }}

Your task:
1. Determine whether travelers of this nationality need a visa to enter the destination country for this purpose and length of stay, based on generally known visa policy (note that policies change, so flag this explicitly).
2. Identify the applicable visa category (Visa-Free, eVisa, Visa on Arrival, Consular Visa, Transit Visa, or Unknown if you are not confident).
3. Recommend the specific visa type/name a traveler in this situation would typically apply for.
4. Flag any eligibility risks, such as insufficient passport validity for the destination's requirements, purpose-visa mismatch, or short-stay limits being exceeded.

Return a JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
{
  "visaRequired": true or false,
  "visaCategory": "Visa-Free|eVisa|Visa on Arrival|Consular Visa|Transit Visa|Unknown",
  "recommendedVisaType": "Name of the specific visa type",
  "maxStayAllowedDays": <number or null>,
  "estimatedProcessingTime": "e.g. 3-5 business days",
  "eligibilityRisks": ["risk1", "risk2"],
  "officialSourceRecommendation": "Brief pointer to verify with the destination country's official embassy/consulate or immigration website",
  "reasoning": "Two to four sentences grounded in the details above",
  "confidence": <number 0-100>
}

If no eligibility risks are found, return an empty array. Return ONLY the JSON. No markdown, no explanation.
